subject: Archaeology
title: 3D Printing Lost Artifacts
description: A quick, practical guide to 3D Printing Lost Artifacts.

hook.text: When ISIS destroyed Palmyra's Arch of Triumph, a team 3D-printed a full-scale replica.

buildup.text: Thousands of tourist photos were processed into a digital 3D model using photogrammetry.

discovery.text: The replica was carved by robotic mills and displayed in London, New York, and Dubai.

twist.text: Critics ask if a replica holds the same value as the original. Is it heritage or a copy?

climax.text: Museums now 3D-print replicas so visitors can touch objects they could never hold.

punchline.text: You can print a copy of a temple. You cannot print its history.

quiz.question: How was the replica of Palmyra's Arch of Triumph created?
options: Archaeologists used original stone blocks from the rubble
Tourist photos were processed into a 3D model for robotic carving
Satellite radar reconstructed the exact dimensions
